plain_what: Instead of turning scores into probabilities and punishing surprise, the loss only asks: does the right answer beat its strongest wrong rivals by a fixed gap? If yes, zero loss and no learning signal. If no, the shortfall in raw score units is the loss. Every step is a comparison and a subtraction.
how_it_works: Float form (offline, pre-D32): for each row take the raw head scores z, find the top-k non-target rivals (k declared in advance, 1 or 8 in the rung-0 arms) and set L = mean over those k of max(0, 1 - z_target + z_rival). Score scale 1 is fixed, a row already leading every rival by 1 contributes exactly zero gradient, and there is no exponential or normalization in either direction. Reports use raw-score measures: top-1, recall at 8, hinge value, unviolated rate. Integer form (current discrete writer): token_hinge T = max(0, width + d(target) - d(best rival token)) using integer L1 token distance, address_hinge A = max(0, 8 + addr(target) - addr(best rival cell)); numerator = 8*T + width*A over 8*width (objective A). Objective R replaces A by R = max(0, r - K) where r is one plus the number of occupied cells that precede the target cell in (address distance, cell id) order, so a crowded cell counts once and R = 0 iff the target cell is among the K kept cells. Eligibility is fixed from the baseline, absent comparisons contribute zero and a wholly ineligible batch refuses with status 8.
geometry: Integer L1 displacement in 8D E8-anchor-orbit blocks, product cells from first/last block root indices (256 cells), address distance to fixed SpiralCore atlas ports, kept-cell count K, exact tie-breaking by smallest token or cell identity. Float form uses negative mean-L1 scores from the shared SpiralCore-port writer.

status_reason: The integer hinge (objectives A and R) is the loss the current discrete writer trains (docs/labs/discrete-geometric-learning-2026-10-13, docs/labs/admission-rank-hinge-2026-10-15). The float rung-0 hinge is READY but was never trained (docs/mechanisms/rank-margin-objective.md). K16-R collapsed occupancy, so the objective choice is open (docs/labs/k16-outcome-call-2026-10-19).

rule_compat.D11: Integer form is already served-compatible: compares, subtractions and integer weights 8 and width (a power-of-two-friendly shift-add). The float form is a training-only objective and its D11 export gap has never been measured.
rule_compat.D23: Compliant by construction: no exp, log-sum-exp, softplus, sigmoid or tanh in either direction. The earlier M2 pooled-rank run used softplus on a log-ratio and is not compliant; it is the historical precursor only.
rule_compat.D30: No matmul. The hinge itself is elementwise; the writer uses integer L1 scans over bounded cell and token sets.
rule_compat.D32_D37: Integer form is the D32 objective. The F32 rung-0 sheet was frozen by D32 item 5 and returns only as a new D37 pre-registration with fresh FIT, owner release, a separately scanned module and a reported export gap.

failed_only_on_configuration: K16-R occupancy collapse: objective R with the seeded 16-vector start and K=16, so one cell holds most tokens and admission passes vacuously; says nothing about hinge objectives with an occupancy term
K16-A admission loss: objective A with K=16 and seeded start; the 16-root start gives an alias ceiling of 1,986 at checkpoint 0
Pilot loss rise: the K=8 weighting of 32 on the address term pushed the total up even as ranks improved; a weighting question, not a ban on margins
Stage A widening: K was changed at evaluation only on a K=8-trained codebook
A4 (Sept 24) and relational reader (Sept 20): older integer-reader margins on constructed panels, where the recipe and the panel, not the margin idea, were the fault
